arxiv-1809-07245.title: Fuzzy Based Wellness Analyzer
arxiv-1809-07245.creator: Rohit Ner, Dibya Prakash Das, Rishabh Kumar, Shubhika Garg
arxiv-1809-07245.description: Abstract Social health and emotional wellness is a matter of concern in today’s urban world. Being the part of a metropolis has an effect on mental health through the influence of increased stressors and factors such as overcrowded and polluted environment, high levels of violence, and reduced social support.

arxiv-2106-04773.title: Virasoro Action on the 𝑸 \boldsymbol{Q} -Functions
arxiv-2106-04773.creator: Kazuya AOKAGE a, Eriko SHINKAWA b and Hiro-Fumi YAMADA c
arxiv-2106-04773.description: Abstract A formula for Schur Q Q -functions is presented which describes the action of the Virasoro operators. For a strict partition, we prove a concise formula for L − k ​ Q λ L_{-k}Q_{\lambda} , where L − k L_{-k} ( k ≥ 1 ) (k\geq 1) is the Virasoro operator.

arxiv-2109-09953.title: From no causal loop to absoluteness of cause: discarding the quantum NOT logic
arxiv-2109-09953.creator: Anandamay Das Bhowmik, Preeti Parashar, Guruprasad Kar, Manik Banik
arxiv-2109-09953.description: Abstract The principle of ‘absoluteness of cause’ (AC) assumes the cause-effect relation to be observer independent and is a distinct assertion than prohibiting occurrence of any causal loop. Here, we study implication of this novel principle to derive a fundamental no-go result in quantum world.

arxiv-2204-07485.title: How to Use K-means for Big Data Clustering? Journal: Pattern Recognition
arxiv-2204-07485.creator: Rustam Mussabayev, Nenad Mladenovic, Ravil Mussabayev, Bassem Jarboui
arxiv-2204-07485.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rustam Mussabayev, Nenad Mladenovic, Ravil Mussabayev, Bassem Jarboui. K-means plays a vital role in data mining and is the simplest and most widely used algorithm under the Euclidean Minimum Sum-of-Squares Clustering (MSSC) model. However, its performance drastically drops when applied to vast amounts of data. Therefore, it is crucial to improve K-means by scaling it to big data using as few of the following computational resources as possible: data, time, and algorithmic ingredients.

arxiv-2208-05465.title: Degenerate r r -Bell polynomials arising from degenerate normal ordering Thanks: * are corresponding authors
arxiv-2208-05465.creator: Taekyun Kim 1,∗, Dae San Kim 2,∗, Hye Kyung Kim 3,∗
arxiv-2208-05465.description: Abstract . Recently, Kim-Kim introduced the degenerate r r -Bell polynomials and investigated some results which are derived from umbral calculus. The aim of this paper is to study some properties of the degenerate r r -Bell polynomials and numbers via boson operators.

arxiv-2304-09406.title: How to Do Things with Deep Learning Code
arxiv-2304-09406.creator: Minh Hua, Rita Raley
arxiv-2304-09406.description: Abstract The premise of this article is that a basic understanding of the composition and functioning of large language models is critically urgent. To that end, we extract a representational map of OpenAI’s GPT-2 with what we articulate as two classes of deep learning code, that which pertains to the model and that which underwrites applications built around the model.

arxiv-2307-13972.title: Scalar Hairy Black Holes with Inverted Mexican Hat Potential
arxiv-2307-13972.creator: Xiao Yan Chew, Kok-Geng Lim
arxiv-2307-13972.description: Abstract We numerically construct the asymptotically flat solutions of hairy black holes supported by a symmetric inverted Mexican hat potential with a local minimum and two degenerate global maxima of a real scalar field that contains a quartic self-interaction term.

arxiv-2311-16974.title: Cole : A Hierarchical Generation Framework for Multi-Layered and Editable Graphic Design
arxiv-2311-16974.creator: Peidong Jia Chenxuan Li Yuhui Yuan Zeyu Liu Yichao Shen Bohan Chen, [0mm] Xingru Chen Yinglin Zheng Dong Chen Ji Li Xiaodong Xie Shanghang Zhang Baining Guo, [0mm] joint core contribution interns at microsoft project lead [1mm] Microsoft Research Asia Peking University {https://graphic-design-genera
arxiv-2311-16974.description: Abstract Graphic design, which has been evolving since the 15th century, plays a crucial role in advertising. The creation of high-quality designs demands design-oriented planning, reasoning, and layer-wise generation . This intricate task involves understanding vague intentions and faithfully generating multi-layered visual elements, including the background, decorations, objects, and fonts, among others.

arxiv-2408-11949.title: Machine learning unveils the materials physical properties driving thermoelectric generators efficiency: half-Heuslers case
arxiv-2408-11949.creator: Anastasiia Tukmakova, Patrizio Graziosi
arxiv-2408-11949.description: Abstract We report the machine learning (ML)–based approach allowing thermoelectric generator (TEG) efficiency evaluation directly from 5 parameters: 2 physical properties – carriers density and energy gap, and 3 engineering parameters – external load resistance, TEG hot side temperature and leg height.

arxiv-2412-05264.title: The neutron veto of the XENONnT experiment: Results with demineralized water
arxiv-2412-05264.creator: E. Aprile addr3, J. Aalbers addr28, K. Abe addr23, S. Ahmed Maouloud addr18, L. Althueser addr7, B. Andrieu addr18, E. Angelino addr14,addr4, D. Antón Martin addr1, F. Arneodo addr9, L. Baudis addr17, M. Bazyk addr13, L. Bellagamba addr0, R. Biondi addr6, A. Bismark addr17, K. Boese addr6, A. Brown
arxiv-2412-05264.description: Abstract Radiogenic neutrons emitted by detector materials are one of the most challenging backgrounds for the direct search of dark matter in the form of weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs). To mitigate this background, the XENONnT experiment is equipped with a novel gadolinium-doped water Cherenkov detector, which encloses the xenon dual-phase time projection chamber (TPC).

arxiv-2502-17588.title: The arc-shaped radio source at the center of NGC 6334A: Is it a colliding wind region of two young massive stars or the bow shock of a runaway star? 2026 The arc-shaped radio source at the center of NGC 6334A: Is it a colliding wind region of two young massive stars or the bow shock of a runaway sta
arxiv-2502-17588.creator: Vanessa Yanza, Sergio A. Dzib, Aina Palau, Luis F. Rodríguez, Josep M. Masqué, Pedro R. Rivera-Ortiz, Sac-Nicté X. Medina
arxiv-2502-17588.description: Abstract New multi-wavelength Karl G. Jansky VLA observations of CKR02A, the compact radio source in the center of the compact HII region NGC 6334A, are presented. The observations were carried out in five epochs and included the frequency ranges 8.0 - 12.0 GHz (X-band), 18.0 - 26.0 GHz (K-band), and 29.0 - 37.0 GHz (Ka-band).

arxiv-2503-17611.title: On continuous polynomials of the Macías space
arxiv-2503-17611.creator: Jhixon Macías
arxiv-2503-17611.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jhixon Macías. Let ℕ \mathbb{N} be the set of natural numbers. The Macías space M ⁡ ( ℕ ) M(\mathbb{N}) is the topological space ( ℕ , τ M ) (\mathbb{N},\tau_{M}) where τ M \tau_{M} is generated by the collection of sets σ n := { m ∈ ℕ : gcd ⁡ ( n , m ) = 1 } \sigma_{n}:=\{m\in\mathbb{N}:\gcd(n,m)=1\} .

arxiv-2509-16386.title: Stokes’ theorem as an entropy-extremizing duality
arxiv-2509-16386.creator: Daniel Lazarev
arxiv-2509-16386.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Daniel Lazarev. Given a manifold ℳ ⊂ ℝ n \mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^{n} , we consider all subsets of ℳ \mathcal{M} that satisfy the generalized Stokes’ theorem and show that ∂ ℳ \partial\mathcal{M} maximizes the associated information theoretic entropy functional. This provides an information theoretic characterization of the duality expressed by Stokes’ theorem, whereby the boundary of a manifold is the ‘least informative’ subset of the manifold satisfying the Stokes relation.

arxiv-2511-11779.title: Bohr phenomena for slice regular functions over Quaternions
arxiv-2511-11779.creator: Sabir Ahammed, Molla Basir Ahamed, Ming-Sheng Liu ∗
arxiv-2511-11779.description: Abstract . Slice regular functions are a generalization of holomorphic functions to the setting of quaternions (and more generally, Clifford algebras). In this paper, we first establish the Bohr inequality for slice starlike functions and slice close-to-convex functions over quaternions ℍ \mathbb{H} .

arxiv-2512-01412.title: A Self-explainable Model of Long Time Series by Extracting Informative Structured Causal Patterns Thanks: Preprint. This version: 2025. Available at arXiv:XXXX.XXXXX.
arxiv-2512-01412.creator: Ziqian Wang, Yuxiao Cheng, Jinli Suo
arxiv-2512-01412.description: Abstract Explainability is essential for neural networks modeling time series data, yet most existing explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques generate point-wise importance scores that overlook intrinsic temporal semantics such as trends, cycles, and abrupt regime changes. This limitation obscures human interpretation and weakens trust in long-sequence models.

arxiv-2512-09063.title: A novel two loop inverse seesaw model
arxiv-2512-09063.creator: Gonzalo Benítez-Irarrázabal, Rocío Branada Balbontín, Cesar Bonilla, A. E. Cárcamo Hernández, Sergey Kovalenko, Juan Marchant González
arxiv-2512-09063.description: Abstract We propose a Standard Model (SM) extension where neutrinos get masses through a two-loop inverse seesaw mechanism. This naturally explains the smallness of the neutrino masses and allows seesaw mediators to be at the TeV scale with testable phenomenology. The model adds two real singlet scalars and four electrically neutral leptons to the SM.

pmc-10666909.title: Carotid Intima-Media Thickness and Its Correlation With Echocardiographic Left Ventricular Function and Geometry in Hypertensive Individuals: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-10666909.creator: Mariam Inuwa, Janet N Ajuluchukwu, Akinsanya Olusegun-Joseph
pmc-10666909.description: BackgroundIt is important to consider left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) in assessing hypertensive patients’ global cardiovascular risk profile, as LVH and arterial wall changes occur concurrently. This study aimed to assess the relationship between CIMT and left ventricular geometry and function in hypertensive patients.

pmc-10743482.title: Signaling in Legume–Rhizobia Symbiosis
pmc-10743482.creator: Julia Shumilina, Alena Soboleva, Evgeny Abakumov, Oksana Y Shtark, Vladimir A Zhukov, Andrej Frolov, Fucheng Lin
pmc-10743482.description: Legumes represent an important source of food protein for human nutrition and animal feed. Therefore, sustainable production of legume crops is an issue of global importance. It is well-known that legume-rhizobia symbiosis allows an increase in the productivity and resilience of legume crops.

pmc-10835789.title: Association between triglyceride glucose index and adverse clinical outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction and LDL-C≤1.8 mmol/L who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention: a prospective cohort study
pmc-10835789.creator: Hong-wei Zhao, Yong Wang, Cheng-fu Wang, Qing-kun Meng
pmc-10835789.description: BackgroundRecently, the triglyceride glucose (TyG) index has emerged as a reliable predictive indicator for adverse outcomes of cardiovascular disease. However, the roles of the TyG index in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)≤1.8 mmol/L after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain unclear.MethodsA total of 599 patients diagnosed with AMI and LDL-C ≤ 1.

pmc-11405040.title: PRMT5-mediated FUBP1 methylation accelerates prostate cancer progression
pmc-11405040.creator: Weiwei Yan, Xun Liu, Xuefeng Qiu, Xuebin Zhang, Jiahui Chen, Kai Xiao, Ping Wu, Chao Peng, Xiaolin Hu, Zengming Wang, Jun Qin, Liming Sun, Luonan Chen, Denglong Wu, Shengsong Huang, Lichen Yin, Zhenfei Li
pmc-11405040.description: Strategies beyond hormone-related therapy need to be developed to improve prostate cancer mortality. Here, we show that FUBP1 and its methylation were essential for prostate cancer progression, and a competitive peptide interfering with FUBP1 methylation suppressed the development of prostate cancer. FUBP1 accelerated prostate cancer development in various preclinical models.

pmc-12377494.title: Functional Brain Reorganization After Radio Electric Asymmetric Conveyer (REAC) Brain Wave Optimization Gamma (BWO-G) Neuromodulation in Individuals With Chronic Stress Exposure: A Retrospective Case Series With Multimodal Evaluation
pmc-12377494.creator: Salvatore Rinaldi, Acary S Oliveira, Valeria Modestto, Arianna Rinaldi, Vania Fontani
pmc-12377494.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Chronic stress exposure is a widespread and disabling condition that disrupts neurophysiological regulation and affects emotional, cognitive, and somatic domains. In this series, the term “chronic stress exposure” refers to prolonged exposure to psychosocial and occupational stressors that, although not classified as a distinct disorder in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition (DSM-5) or International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10), can induce persistent dysregulation of brain networks involved in emotion and cognition.

pmc-12512691.title: Stomatal anatomy and gas exchange dynamics in the Brachypodium distachyon complex
pmc-12512691.creator: Lea S. Berg, Alexander Betekhtin, Anna Milewska-Hendel, Michael T. Raissig
pmc-12512691.description: Stomata, the epidermal pores enabling gas exchange and transpiration, are crucial for plant fitness and global water and carbon cycling. Grasses possess efficient four-celled, graminoid stomatal complexes, where dumbbell-shaped guard cells (GCs) and lateral subsidiary cells (SCs) enable rapid stomatal movements.

pmc-12574101.title: Developing items for inclusion in a new pain-specific patient-reported outcome measure for pelvic floor surgery: a mixed-methods study
pmc-12574101.creator: Sheymonti S Hoque, Susannah Ahern, Helen E O’Connell, Rasa Ruseckaite
pmc-12574101.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundWomen undergoing pelvic floor procedures (PFPs) to treat their pelvic floor disorder (PFD) may experience pain, affecting their health-related quality of life. Current patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) assess pain but are not specific to PFD post-surgery.

pmc-12723837.title: Implementing incentives in family medicine for opioid use disorder treatment: a qualitative inquiry on provider and patient preferences for a low magnitude reward program compatible with buprenorphine treatment
pmc-12723837.creator: Samantha Ellis, Jax Witzig, Diego Basaldu, Brittany Rudd, Nicole Gastala, Alexandra R Tabachnick, Sungha Kang, Tondalaya Henry, Nathan Stackhouse, Margaret Wardle
pmc-12723837.description: BackgroundIncentive programs are an effective yet underutilized behavioral intervention that can improve outcomes in medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD) treatment. Contingency Management (CM) is a rigorous incentive program run per seven evidence-based principles (e.g. objectively verifiable target behaviors, frequent opportunities for incentives).

pmc-12738770.title: Argonaute-HNH filaments triggered by invader DNA confer bacterial immunity
pmc-12738770.creator: Anna Kanevskaya, Manju Narwal, Lidiya Lisitskaya, Andrey V. Moiseenko, Olga S. Sokolova, Nikolai N. Sluchanko, Katsuhiko S. Murakami, Andrey Kulbachinskiy
pmc-12738770.description: Argonaute proteins provide innate immunity in all domains of life through guide-dependent recognition and cleavage of invader nucleic acids. Many short prokaryotic Argonautes (pAgos) lack nuclease activity and are instead co-encoded with tentative nuclease effectors, but their activation mechanisms remain unknown. Here, we characterize SPARHA systems (short prokaryotic argonautes, HNH-associated), containing HNH nuclease effectors.

pmc-13060201.title: A Blueprint for Improving the Research Infrastructure of a Pediatric Hospital Medicine Division
pmc-13060201.creator: Gina L Gallizzi, Tamara L Gayle, Anand Gourishankar, Kavita Parikh, Margaret L Rush, Amina Touma, Susan C Walley, Priti Bhansali
pmc-13060201.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: While research barriers in academic medical practice have been identified in prior studies, the facilitators and barriers to research productivity for pediatric hospital medicine (PHM) faculty in the era of board certification are not well described.Objectives: This study aimed to (1) identify the perceived facilitators and barriers to research productivity among PHM faculty at a large tertiary care children’s hospital, and (2) explore potential differences between fellowship-trained and non-fellowship-trained faculty in their perceptions of the facilitators and barriers to research.Methodology: A

pmc-13146691.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1241 NURSE-LED TRIAGE OF PRE-HOSPITAL STROKE CODES REDUCES EASILY RECOGNIZED MIMICS WITHOUT AFFECTING STROKE YIELD
pmc-13146691.creator: Michael Teitcher, Nechama Polak, Roni Eichel, Natan Bornstein, Stefan Mausbach
pmc-13146691.description: Background and aimsPre-hospital stroke code activation by emergency medical services (EMS) is essential for timely treatment in the emergency department (ED) but is frequently triggered by non-stroke conditions (“stroke mimics”). A protocol-driven pilot program was implemented allowing ED nurses to cancel pre-hospital activated stroke codes when predefined criteria were met for non-stroke presentations or acute treatment ineligibility.

pmc-13382411.title: Paternal genetic background orchestrates fetal development through tissue-specific cis-regulatory divergence
pmc-13382411.creator: Muhammad Arsalan Iqbal, Eduard Murani, Frieder Hadlich, Henry Reyer, Michael Oster, Nares Trakooljul, Klaus Wimmers, Siriluck Ponsuksili
pmc-13382411.description: SummaryPaternal influences on offspring development extend beyond Mendelian inheritance, but how sire genetics shape fetal transcription and cis-regulatory landscapes across tissues is unclear. Using a reciprocal backcross in pigs (F1×German Landrace vs. F1×Piétrain) and a haplotype-agnostic RNA-seq pipeline, we profiled six fetal tissues to test sire-breed effects. We identified paternal breed-driven transcriptional divergence, with 1,176 genes differentially expressed.

pmc-13593086.title: Association between the oxidative balance score and gynecologic cancers from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey: An observational study
pmc-13593086.creator: Ya'nan Yan, Lei Zhang, Shuai Yuan, Ting Zhang, Can Shi
pmc-13593086.description: This study aimed to examine the potential correlations between the oxidative balance score (OBS) and gynecological cancers susceptibility. A cross-sectional design was employed, utilizing datasets from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey spanning 2 decades from 1999 through 2018. Our investigation demonstrated that OBS exhibited significant protective correlations with gynecologic cancers (odds ratio [OR]=0.985, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.974–0.

pmc-13594472.title: Preclinical assessment of a novel ablation catheter specific to robotic magnetic navigation
pmc-13594472.creator: Qingzhi Luo, Xiang Li, Yangyang Bao, Changjian Lin, Yun Xie, Yue Wei, Tianyou Ling, Ning Zhang, Kang Chen, Wenqi Pan, Liqun Wu, Qi Jin
pmc-13594472.description: BackgroundA novel catheter (Magbot) is needed to enable seamless integration with robotic magnetic navigation systems and third-party mapping platforms.ObjectiveThe goals of this study were to assess the contact force (CF) and lesion characteristics of the Magbot catheter under robotic magnetic navigation guidance and to compare these parameters with those of the RMT catheter solely for the CARTO system.
